dctx

Choose your path • Which mode? • Philosophy • Installation • Quick Start • Output examples • Library • Map mode • Security & Privacy • Specification • Website

dctx turns any folder into the smallest correct context for a task, offline, with byte-stable output that prompt caches can reuse.
dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts the context an agent needs to a fraction. Used without a plan, it can add calls and tokens instead of removing them. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything.

--- ## Installation **System binary — available now.** Download the archive for your OS and architecture from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/releases/tag/v1.3.0), compare its SHA-256 with the matching entry in `SHA256SUMS`, extract it, and put `dctx` (`dctx.exe` on Windows) on `PATH`. Archives cover Linux x64/ARM64, macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64. Releases after 1.2.0 also ship cosign signatures, a CycloneDX SBOM, build provenance and offline bundles; see [verification, provenance and offline installation](docs/VERIFYING.md). ```sh dctx --version ``` **Project wrappers — built and tested in CI, registry publication pending.** The [Python](packages/python/README.md), [Node](packaging/npm/dctx/README.md) and [Go](packages/go/README.md) wrappers over `dctx rpc` are built and tested in CI, but nothing is published to PyPI, npm, crates.io or a Go module proxy yet. Until then, a `dctx` package on those registries is not from this project. The [Rust facade](docs/MODALITIES.md#rust-library-embed-the-facade) is available from tagged Git. Use the release archives for the CLI. Follow [the safe path in ten minutes](docs/START.md#safe-path-in-ten-minutes) for one project, lean MCP setup and whole-session measurement. ## What the output looks like These are real runs on the tiny [kiosk sample](tools/website/sample), captured by [capture.py](tools/website/capture.py) from the release binary. Commands run inside a copy named `kiosk`. For source builds, the executable is `dctx-cli` (or define a `dctx` alias). ### Pack a project The header explains the format, the tree assigns IDs, and file blocks carry paths and line counts. The first 40 output lines follow; only the tail is omitted. `.env` is listed without its contents. ```text $ dctx pack . [DCTX_LLM_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT_V1] [DIRECTORY:kiosk] 1. the footer reports usage and dropped records. ```text $ dctx pack . --for 'greet store' --budget 800 # dctx pack --for budget=800 terms=2 ## find greet s:src/util.rs#greet fn L2-4 s:web/app.ts#renderGreeting fn L10-12 ## find store s:src/store.rs#Order struct L4-8 s:src/store.rs#checksum fn L22-24 s:src/store.rs#encode fn L17-19 ## neighbors s:src/util.rs#greet calls:in:s:src/main.rs#main fn src/main.rs L7 calls:out:s:src/util.rs#title_case fn src/util.rs contains:in:m:src/util.rs module src/util.rs ## neighbors s:src/store.rs#Order contains:in:m:src/store.rs module src/store.rs ## read s:src/util.rs#greet s:src/util.rs#greet fn src/util.rs pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String { format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name)) } ## read s:src/store.rs#Order s:src/store.rs#Order struct src/store.rs pub struct Order { pub id: u32, pub item: String, pub qty: u32, } # end body_tokens=223 budget=800 dropped=0 ``` ## Which mode? - [CLI and one-off chat](docs/MODALITIES.md#human-one-off-pack-to-clipboard): pack selected source for a prompt or use the interactive terminal. - [Agents, short tasks](docs/MODALITIES.md#short-agent-task-grep-can-be-enough): compare with grep plus narrow file reads first. - [Agents, long sessions and huge trees](docs/MODALITIES.md#huge-trees-scope-before-indexing): scope the root, find symbols and read exact source. - [MCP](docs/guides/MCP.md): use the lean profile to start; ACP is planned. - [Libraries](docs/MODALITIES.md#rust-library-embed-the-facade): embed the Rust facade today; the [Python, Node and Go wrappers](docs/MODALITIES.md#python-node-and-go-wrappers-registry-publication-pending) are built and tested in CI, with registry publication pending. - [CI and prompt caching](docs/MODALITIES.md#ci--prompt-cache-prefix-stability): pin inputs and measure byte stability and provider cache behavior. - [Desktop](docs/MODALITIES.md#desktop-app-tauri-preview-today): build the Tauri 0.11 preview; the GPUI rebuild is planned. ## Measured, in the open The baseline is **grep plus reading files**. A controlled grep-plus-read benchmark that counts whole agent sessions (start-up context, every call, provider cache hits and accuracy) is being prepared; until it is published, dctx makes no whole-session savings claim. Historical cold indexing of six benchmark corpora took dctx 0.13–1.20 s on one Linux x86_64 runner. This measures CLI wall time, not agent completion time or session cost. [Choosing how to use dctx](docs/MODALITIES.md) covers scoping and MCP startup overhead. [Measurement evidence](docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md) describes what was measured (tool-output bytes and estimated tokens); other-tool protocols are retained only as secondary historical notes. ## Start and choose your path [What dctx is](docs/START.md), [four user paths](docs/START.md#choose-your-path), [responsibilities](docs/START.md#responsibilities), and [two scopes, one binary](docs/START.md#two-scopes-one-binary) explain setup and ownership. The [documentation index](docs/README.md) groups modalities, scopes, engine behavior, reference material, trust and evaluator evidence. “Smallest correct context” is the goal: selection is lexical and bounded, not a proof of task completeness or a mathematical minimum. Large folders need scoped roots; budgets bound answers, not scans. Provider cache hits and whole-session savings must be measured. See [current limits](docs/MODALITIES.md) and the [specification and roadmap](docs/SPEC.md). ## The core belief: prompt-processing efficiency Send fewer relevant bytes, keep their order stable, and verify exact source. dctx does not use embeddings; it selects lexical symbols and document sections. - **Bounded**: map answers use estimated token budgets and whole records. - **Deterministic**: identical source snapshots and requests give identical bytes. Read the [philosophy](docs/WHY-DCTX.md) and its [testable constraints](docs/SPEC.md#2-the-core-belief-prompt-processing-efficiency). ## Quick Start Try a tiny project (POSIX shell; on Windows use Git Bash): ```sh mkdir dctx-demo cd dctx-demo printf 'def hello(name):\n return f"Hello, {name}!"\n' > hello.py dctx map skeleton hello.py ``` Use the [safe path](docs/START.md#safe-path-in-ten-minutes) or the [runnable pack and map example](examples/README.md). For repeated agent work, see [Map mode: context for agents](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md) and the [MCP client guide](docs/guides/MCP.md). ## Map mode: context for agents From this repository's root: ```zsh dctx map find "Session" ``` Read exact IDs from the result with `dctx map read 'ID' --json`. See the [map guide](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md) for commands, budgets and limits. ## From source Requires Rust 1.91 or newer. ```sh git clone https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx cd dctx cargo build --locked --release -p dctx-cli ./target/release/dctx-cli --version alias dctx="$PWD/target/release/dctx-cli" ``` Cargo builds `dctx-cli` (`dctx-cli.exe` on Windows); release archives supply `dctx`. For a local source installation, use `cargo install --locked --path crates/dctx-cli` and `alias dctx=dctx-cli`. On Windows, invoke the executable directly or create a PowerShell alias. See [CI coverage and desktop exclusions](docs/TESTING.md). ## Use as a library The public Rust entry point is the [`dctx` facade](crates/dctx), available from Git now; **crates.io publication is pending**. ```toml [dependencies] dctx = { git = "https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx", tag = "v1.3.0" } ``` This example is generated from the [workspace doctest](examples/library/README.md): ```rust use dctx::{memory::{CancelFlag, FixedClock, MemorySource}, *}; let mut source = MemorySource::new(); source.insert_file("hello.rs", b"pub fn hello() {}\n", 0)?; let mut session = Session::builder(source).clock(FixedClock(Timestamp(0))) .cancellation(std::sync::Arc::new(CancelFlag::new())).ceiling(HostCeiling::base()) .selection(SelectionPolicy::from_texts(&RuleTexts::default())).grants(HostGrants::PermitAll) .storage(StoragePolicy::Ephemeral { max_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }).place("demo").view("pack").build()?; let mut output = VecSink::new(); session.pack(&PackRequest::new(), &mut output)?; println!("{}", std::str::from_utf8(output.as_bytes())?); ``` The host supplies selection rules and storage policy; `FsSource` does not load `.gitignore` automatically. Read the [library integration boundary](docs/MODALITIES.md#rust-library-embed-the-facade) before embedding it. Python, Node and Go wrappers over `dctx rpc` live in [packages/python](packages/python/README.md), [packaging/npm](packaging/npm/dctx/README.md) and [packages/go](packages/go/README.md); they are built and tested in CI, and registry publication is pending. ## CLI Reference ``` Usage: dctx [OPTIONS] dctx pack [PATH] [--output PATH] [--clipboard] [--json] dctx pack [PATH] --for [--budget TOKENS] dctx map [--json] dctx context TARGET [--place PATH] [--budget N] [--json] [--session ID --dedupe] dctx rpc dctx mcp [PATH] dctx serve [--mcp] [PATH] dctx read [OPTIONS] dctx languages [--json|--markdown] dctx doctor [--json] dctx cache status [--json] [--root PATH] dctx cache gc [--dry-run] [--root PATH] [--max-bytes N] dctx cache purge --root PATH [--dry-run] [--yes] dctx cache purge --all [--dry-run] [--yes] dctx cache config [auto on|off] [--max-bytes N] [--ttl-days N] dctx cache auto [--json] dctx template build [--output PATH] dctx template list [--dir PATH] dctx plugin search|install|list|info|enable|disable|remove|update|verify dctx git Pack filters: --ext Only files with these extensions (comma-separated) --binary Include binary files (omitted by default) --empty Only 0-byte files --non-empty Only files with content --large Only files larger than this many megabytes --small Only files smaller than this many megabytes --hidden Only hidden files and directories --debug-ignored List ignored directories without reading them --include Only files matching this ignore-rule glob (repeatable) --exclude Drop files matching this ignore-rule glob (repeatable) --output, -o Write the page to one file --clipboard, -c Copy the page to the clipboard --json Summary report; Call edges are lexical, not type-resolved: they come from names, scopes and imports, never from a type checker, and ambiguous references are dropped. - **outline**: symbols only; no call edges are promised. ## Security & Privacy Pack, map and MCP run locally and have **no telemetry**, **call no model** and **make no network calls**. Selection happens before any byte is read, hashed, parsed or cached, and is checked again before output leaves the engine. | Rule file | Behaviour | |---|---| | `.gitignore`, `.dctxignore`, global ignore file | Excluded from normal selection; `--debug-ignored` shows ignored path metadata without reading content | The global ignore file is `/dctx/ignore`: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dctx/ignore` or `~/.config/dctx/ignore` on Linux and macOS, `%APPDATA%\dctx\ignore` on Windows. dctx does not read Git metadata, so `.git/info/exclude` and Git's `core.excludesFile` are **not** applied: copy those patterns into `.dctxignore` or the global ignore file when they must keep files out of a pack. `DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1` skips those ignore texts, so leave it unset when relying on them. Built-in sensitive-file and `.git` exclusions still apply. Sensitive files such as `.env`, private keys and credentials are omitted from content reads even with ignore negations; pack may list their names. `.git` at any depth is never listed or read by map, and is never read by pack. Symlinks are never followed; final-component file opens use `O_NOFOLLOW`. dctx decides by file name only: a secret pasted into an ordinary source file is not detected. Inspect context before sharing it. The [privacy contract and deny list](docs/ADR-014-Privacy-Guarantees-and-Ignore-Semantics.md) and [map privacy guide](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md#index-cache-and-privacy) explain the boundary. Report vulnerabilities privately through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). The [release check](scripts/release-check.sh) tests socket activity under `strace -f` and reports SKIP where tracing cannot run. Plugin network and organization policy designs in the spec include planned features; see [current plugin limits](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md#what-is-not-yet-available). ## Open source and maintenance dctx and its desktop app are [Apache-2.0](LICENSE), copyright Eris Margeta. Every modality stays open. [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/Eris-Margeta) and [maintenance agreements](MAINTENANCE.md) fund upkeep without changing the license. The local clipboard must be available. To inspect or save the same selection instead: ```sh dctx pack . --output context.txt ``` Do not use an unbounded whole-project pack for a large tree or when only one function matters. Narrow the root first, or use map reads. Pack's `--ext rs,toml` and `--small 1` filters can restrict extensions and file sizes (MB); they are pack filters, not map index limits. Inspect the content before sharing it. ## Short agent task: grep can be enough If you know a name and expect only a few file reads, use the existing shell: ```sh grep -R -n -F --include='*.rs' 'struct Session' crates/dctx/src sed -n '130,170p' crates/dctx/src/session/mod.rs ``` Choose the line range from the search result; reading a narrow range is an honest baseline alongside whole-file reads. If a symbol read is useful, call `dctx map find Session` through the existing shell. Loading an MCP server adds tool descriptions to starting context; installing verbose agent instructions can add more. Do not add that setup for a tiny edit unless you measure a benefit. ```sh cd crates/dctx-lex-go dctx map find Add --budget 500 --limit 5 dctx map read 's:tests/fixtures/basic.go#Add' --json dctx map skeleton tests/fixtures/basic.go --budget 1000 ``` For your project, use the exact ID returned by `find`. Both text `read` and `read --json` include verified source bytes; JSON carries them in `source_utf8`. Skeletons show declaration signatures without bodies. If an answer has `more` and `next`, pass that opaque `next` value with `--cursor` on the same request, and count the extra call. Budgets are estimated output tokens, not a model tokenizer promise. ## Huge trees: scope before indexing A 100 GB+ folder, including a 200 GB working tree, is a container of possible scopes, not a promise that dctx can index it all at once. Source volume, visited entries, record count and cache size are separate limits. Markdown headings produce document nodes, so mostly text trees can still have large indexes. Map's shared cache stores a lifecycle ledger (`ledger.v1`), policy (`policy.v1`), serialized generations and their view manifests in managed object files. A map generation contains file inventory, digests and stat stamps, declarations, summaries, signatures, source spans and edges. It is not a copy of the whole source tree or an embedding store; exact source reads still verify live files. A compatible unchanged generation can be reused across CLI processes. The product hard cap is **2 GiB (2,147,483,648 accounted bytes)** across the shared cache. Defaults also include a 1.5 GiB soft watermark and a roughly 1.2 GiB cleanup target. Admission evicts reclaimable generations first, preserving live reader leases. If the new generation still cannot fit, the query fails with a cache-limit error; it does not quietly return a complete partial index. Repeating the same unscoped request will not fix this. The cap is not a RAM-usage or exact filesystem-size guarantee. `cache config --max-bytes` can only tighten it. Start at the relevant package, not the huge parent: ```sh cd packages/service-a dctx map find Config --budget 500 --limit 5 # Equivalent root selection from elsewhere: dctx map find Config --place packages/service-a --budget 500 --limit 5 ``` `--place` selects the scan root. `--in src` narrows find/grep matches **after** indexing; `--budget`, `--limit` and `--cursor` bound answers, not the tree scan. Running from a subfolder changes relative paths and IDs; retain the needed ignore rules there instead of assuming parent project rules were inherited. Use existing `.gitignore` and a `.dctxignore` at the chosen root to exclude data, generated output and irrelevant documents before reads, parsing and caching. For example, merge these project-specific entries into `.dctxignore`: ```gitignore /data/ /generated/ /archive/ ``` The host loads the global ignore file, root and nested `.gitignore` rules, then the root `.dctxignore`. Built-in sensitive-file and `.git` exclusions still apply. The global ignore file is `/dctx/ignore`: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dctx/ignore` or `~/.config/dctx/ignore` on Linux and macOS, `%APPDATA%\dctx\ignore` on Windows. dctx does not read Git metadata, so `.git/info/exclude` and Git's `core.excludesFile` are not applied; put those patterns in `.dctxignore` or the global ignore file. Do not set `DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1` when relying on these ignore rules. The built binary documents these **environment variables**, not scan-limit flags: | Variable | Default | Accepted range / effect | |---|---|---| | `DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` | 1,073,741,824 (1 GiB) | 1–17,179,869,184 total source bytes per scan | | `DCTX_MAX_RECORDS` | 1,000,000 | 1–100,000,000 files, symbols and edges | | `DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES` | 100,000 | 1–100,000,000 visited files and directories | For a deliberately smaller scope and fail-fast ceilings: ```sh DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES=268435456 DCTX_MAX_RECORDS=250000 DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES=25000 \ dctx map find Config --place packages/service-a --budget 500 --limit 5 dctx cache status --json dctx cache gc --dry-run ``` Limits refuse an oversized scan; they do not produce an exhaustive answer from a truncated scan. Raising source or record ceilings does not raise the 2 GiB cache cap. A different absolute `DCTX_CACHE_DIR` selects a separate cache location, not a larger cap. Do not use dctx on the whole huge tree if narrowing would exclude facts your task requires; use grep and direct reads across the needed directories, or query several explicit scopes and account for extra calls. ## MCP server: convenient tools with startup context Configure your MCP client to launch this process in the selected project root: ```sh dctx mcp . ``` ### Client configuration Install the CLI archive first. Replace both absolute paths below with your executable and the project to index (on Windows, use `dctx.exe` and JSON-escaped paths). An explicit project path avoids relying on the client's working directory. For a source build, point `command` at `target/release/dctx-cli`. [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) (`.mcp.json` at the project root) and [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp) (`.cursor/mcp.json`) use this JSON: ```json { "mcpServers": { "dctx": { "type": "stdio", "command": "/absolute/path/to/dctx", "args": ["mcp", "/absolute/path/to/project"] } } } ``` [Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/) uses `~/.codex/config.toml` (or `.codex/config.toml` in a trusted project): ```toml [mcp_servers.dctx] command = "/absolute/path/to/dctx" args = ["mcp", "/absolute/path/to/project"] ``` ### Tools and startup cost It exposes ten tools: `map`, `find`, `neighbors`, `explain`, `read`, `skeleton`, `grep`, `hubs`, `path`, `export`. These are query tools, not a pack or cache-admin interface. Export emits the whole graph without the normal answer-token cap. Both text and JSON `read` answers include verified source bytes. Set the MCP `read` argument `"json": true` for structured output with `source_utf8`, equivalent to the CLI's `--json`. | Payload | Exact UTF-8 bytes | Estimated tokens | |---|---|---| | Complete `tools/list` response, request ID `2`, without trailing LF | 6,135 | 1,753 | | Same response including one LF | 6,136 | — | | Compact `result.tools` array alone (definitions and schemas) | 6,091 | 1,741 | The [captured response](assets/mcp-tools-list-1.2.0.json) includes its trailing LF. Token estimates use `ceil(2 × bytes / 7)`, the CLI's byte heuristic, **not an actual model tokenizer**. Clients may transform schemas, add wrappers or defer loading tools, so this is the definition payload's estimated startup cost, not the client's exact input-token count. Reproduce from the project root (with `dctx` on PATH): ```sh python3 - <<'PYCODE' import json import subprocess requests = [ {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize", "params": { "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "dctx-modality-measurement", "version": "1"}}}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"}, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/list"}, ] wire = "".join(json.dumps(r, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n" for r in requests) reply = subprocess.run(["dctx", "mcp", "."], input=wire.encode(), stdout=subprocess.PIPE, check=True).stdout line = next(x for x in reply.splitlines() if json.loads(x).get("id") == 2) definitions = json.dumps(json.loads(line)["result"]["tools"], ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode() for name, payload in [("response without LF", line), ("tools array", definitions)]: print(name, len(payload), "bytes;", (2 * len(payload) + 6) // 7, "est. tokens") PYCODE ``` Do not enable MCP solely to save output tokens on a short task. Prefer existing shell access when it avoids adding definitions; use MCP when the client's tool workflow makes repeated focused queries useful. Compare total session usage under the same client and model, including definition loading and extra turns. ## CI / prompt-cache prefix stability Save deterministic output from a fixed selection as a build artifact: ```sh dctx pack . --output context.txt dctx map find Session --json > symbol-context.json ``` Keep generated artifacts outside the next scan or ignore them. Keep the default `--tree-stamps=off` for stable prefixes. For map, leave `--meta` off to exclude changing snapshot, generation and age metadata. Keep stable instructions and context early in the assembled prompt, followed by changing task text. Use the same template, root, request and binary version. The [stability report](research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md) measured 33/33 text and 33/33 JSON answers unchanged after unrelated edits on three Linux corpora, and identical output over five runs. It measured answer bytes, not provider cache hits, billed tokens or whole-session latency. A bare `touch` leaves default pack output unchanged; a real edit can preserve the bytes before the edited file. Do not assume every edit preserves the entire prompt, or that provider cache retention and minimum-prefix requirements are controlled by dctx. ## Rust library: embed the facade The supported entry point for Rust integrations is the [`dctx` facade](../crates/dctx), which exposes `Session`, `SnapshotRequest`, `MapRequest`, `PackRequest`, sinks, templates and cache operations. The facade does not discover a home directory, global configuration, Git executable or plugin host; it does not print to stdout. The example's `println!` belongs to the caller. Use the Rust facade when you need an in-process engine. # What dctx is dctx turns any folder into the smallest correct context for a task, offline, with byte-stable output that prompt caches can reuse. “Smallest correct context” describes the goal, not a proof that task selection is complete or minimal. The shipped engine selects lexical symbols and document sections, verifies source reads and bounds answers. A 200 GB folder needs a relevant sub-root and ignore rules; output budgets do not bound scanning. Byte stability enables reuse, while provider cache rules determine actual hits. dctx has no embeddings, network, telemetry or agent loop in its pack/map/MCP workflows. It does not call a model or execute the task for you. > dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts the context an agent needs to a fraction. Used without a plan, it can add calls and tokens instead of removing them. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything. ## Choose your path Choose one of these four paths. Each starts with a shipped workflow; the planned scope and distribution features are labeled explicitly. 1. Install the system binary Download the archive for your OS and architecture and `SHA256SUMS` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/releases/tag/v1.3.0). Compare the archive's SHA-256 with its matching entry before extracting it. On Linux use `sha256sum ARCHIVE`, on macOS `shasum -a 256 ARCHIVE`, or on Windows PowerShell `Get-FileHash ARCHIVE -Algorithm SHA256`, replacing `ARCHIVE` with the downloaded filename. Archives cover Linux x64/ARM64, macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64. ```sh dctx --version ``` Use the system binary for interactive agents. The project wrappers (Python, Node, Go) are built and tested in CI, with registry publication pending; no project dependency is needed for this path. ### 2. Choose one project and inspect one answer Use a small project or a relevant sub-root. Check `.gitignore` and `.dctxignore` before scanning; leave `DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED` unset. From that directory: ```sh dctx map find Config --json --budget 500 --limit 5 ``` Replace `Config` with a symbol or heading in your project. Read a returned ID with `dctx map read 'ID' --json`. The JSON includes verified source bytes as `source_utf8` and reports precision, freshness and pagination. Keep the same root between calls, because root-relative IDs change when the root changes. ### 3. Configure the lean MCP profile In a client accepting `mcpServers`, replace both absolute paths: ```json { "mcpServers": { "dctx": { "command": "/absolute/path/to/dctx", "args": ["mcp", "--profile", "lean", "/absolute/path/to/project"] } } } ``` Restart the client and confirm that `find` and `read` are available. The lean profile has **two tools**, not the planned `context/read/find` profile. For a controlled comparison, turn off overlapping host file tools where the client allows it; keep instructions and task scope consistent. Use the [MCP guide](guides/MCP.md) for profile selection and measured startup overhead, and [client-specific configs](MODALITIES.md#client-configuration) for other formats. ### 4. Measure before changing anything Run the same small task with grep plus narrow file reads and with lean MCP. Record task correctness, number of tool calls, startup instructions and schemas, all model input/output tokens, provider cache hits, latency and billed cost when available. Include the history carried into each model turn. Smaller tool answers alone do not establish whole-session savings. General receipts are planned. Today, retain JSON metadata and the agent's usage report. For task packs, the shipped footer is a useful output accounting line: ```sh dctx pack . --for 'Config' --budget 800 ``` It reports `body_tokens`, `budget` and `dropped`, using estimated tokens rather than a provider tokenizer. It is not a whole-session receipt. Save outputs outside the selected tree, and compare repeated runs with identical inputs. Continue with the [documentation index](README.md), [modalities](MODALITIES.md) or [engine specification](SPEC.md). # Why dctx exists What problem dctx solves, the rules it follows, and why "byte-identical output" matters even if you never think about bytes. ## The problem An AI coding assistant only knows what is in its **context window**: the text sent to the model with your request. It cannot see the rest of your project. Most projects are too large to send whole, so tools pick pieces. Often they pick badly: whole files when one function would do, text that looks similar but is the wrong code, code as it was before your last edit, or half a function. Each of these costs you. Models read text as **tokens** (small chunks of text, roughly a short word or part of one), and providers bill per token. The model reads every token before it answers, so more tokens also means more waiting. And answers get worse as irrelevant text piles up. The [README](../README.md#the-core-belief-prompt-processing-efficiency) sums it up: every token in front of a model is paid for three times, to read it, again when a cache is missed, and again in attention. ## What dctx does dctx is a command-line tool that reads your project on your machine and answers precise questions about it: where a function is defined, what calls it, what its exact source is. Each answer fits a size budget and is built from whole pieces of syntax; a piece that is too long is marked as cut, with a way to get the rest. The same question about the same code gives the same bytes every time. An assistant can run the commands itself or call them through the built-in MCP server (`dctx mcp`; MCP is a standard way for AI tools to call other tools). dctx can also pack a whole project into one structured block for a chat. ### Start with grep plus file reads The baseline is a literal search followed by reading the relevant files or line ranges. That is often enough for a short task. dctx earns its place when exact symbol reads and outlines avoid repeatedly sending large, irrelevant files. It aims to be one context-management tool across these workflows; choose the surface that fits in [Choosing how to use dctx](MODALITIES.md). ### A small worked example Run with dctx 1.1.0 on a copy of this repository's `crates/dctx-lex-go` folder. The output is real and complete. ```text $ dctx map find Add # dctx-lex-go find s:tests/fixtures/basic.go#Add fn L43-45 $ dctx map read 's:tests/fixtures/basic.go#Add' # dctx-lex-go read s:tests/fixtures/basic.go#Add fn tests/fixtures/basic.go func Add[T ~int](a, b T) T { return a } $ dctx map neighbors 's:tests/fixtures/basic.go#Add' --edge calls --dir in # dctx-lex-go neighbors calls:in:s:tests/fixtures/basic.go#main fn tests/fixtures/basic.go L59 ``` `find` returns a stable id, the kind of thing it is (a function) and its lines. This is a historical 1.1.0 transcript; the current CLI also includes verified source bytes in text `read` output, or in `source_utf8` with `read --json`. `neighbors` says that `main` calls it, on line 59. ## The philosophy The [specification](SPEC.md#2-the-core-belief-prompt-processing-efficiency) turns this into five testable rules. **Bounded.** Every map answer has a size ceiling, reserved before anything is written, and a record is never split. The budget is up to 2,000 estimated tokens (1,000 for `explain`). *Why it matters to you:* one question cannot flood the context window and crowd out your own instructions. **Deterministic.** The same code and the same question give the same bytes. *Why it matters to you:* results are repeatable, and repeated prompts can be served from a cache. **Prefix-stable.** When context is sent again across turns, bytes that did not need to change do not change. *Why it matters to you:* this is what keeps caching working across a conversation. **Non-redundant.** Within one session, do not resend what was already sent unless it changed. This one is still a target. **Honest.** Every answer states its freshness, precision and provenance, and dctx never asserts what it does not know. With `--json`, the `read` above carries `"freshness":{"mode":"strict","state":"verified"}`, a `precision` block, and `more` and `next` fields for anything that did not fit. Calls it cannot resolve are listed as `unresolved`, not guessed. *Why it matters to you:* you and your assistant can tell a fact from a guess. The docs add a few more commitments: - **Offline.** No telemetry, no update checks, no model calls. A release check counted zero network connections across 16 commands. Nothing leaves your machine. - **Private by default.** A file is classified before any byte of it is read. Secret-shaped files such as `.env`, `*.pem` and `id_rsa` are listed with content omitted, with no override in v1. - **No embeddings.** dctx does not turn code into vectors and search by similarity. It ranks by names and syntax. - **Features must earn their place.** A feature without a measured acceptance gate is not a dctx feature. ## Why byte-identical output matters ### Prompt caching, in plain words Much of each request to an AI model repeats the last one: system instructions, project context, earlier turns. Providers keep a cache of prompt beginnings. If the **start** of a new prompt matches a cached one exactly, byte for byte, they reuse their earlier work on that part. Cached input costs a fraction of the normal price and is processed faster. The match must be exact, and it is checked from the beginning. Picture a reader who remembers the first fifty pages you sent earlier. Send the same fifty pages and they skip ahead. Change one word on page two, and from that word on they must read everything again, even if pages three to fifty are unchanged. So one changed byte early in a prompt (a timestamp, a file listed in a different order, a file size) breaks the cache for everything after it. ### Prefix-stable, simply "Prefix" means the beginning of a text. "Prefix-stable" means the beginning stays the same unless the content there really changed. Edit one file, and only the bytes from that file onward should differ. Timestamps are the classic problem. In 1.0.0, every line of the `dctx pack` file tree carried a modification time, and file lines a size. The tree sits near the top, so merely re-saving a file (a `touch`) changed almost the whole page as far as a cache is concerned. Since 1.1.0 tree lines carry only an id. A bare `touch` leaves the output byte-identical, and an edit keeps everything before the edited file as a shared prefix. `--tree-stamps=on` brings back the old lines. In the same folder we appended one comment line to the last file in the tree, `tests/review_lexers_a.rs`, and compared `dctx pack .` before and after: ```text default output: first 117,215 of 122,437 bytes unchanged --tree-stamps=on: first 2,151 of 123,159 bytes unchanged ``` By default about 96% of the page is still a reusable prefix. With timestamps on, almost nothing is. ### The evidence The [stability report](research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md) measured map answers on 6 November 2026, on three pinned local corpora with 11 kinds of question each. **33 of 33** text answers and **33 of 33** JSON answers were byte-identical after an unrelated edit elsewhere in the project, and all were identical over five separate runs. The report states its limits too. It measures dctx's answers, not a provider's cache hits. It ran on Linux only. The layered design that would keep context prefix-stable across a whole conversation ([SPEC §12.1](SPEC.md#121-prefix-stable-tiers-target)) is still a target. ### An illustration of money and time *Made-up numbers, not any provider's prices.* Assume: - an agent sends the same 20,000 tokens of project context on each of 10 turns; - normal input costs 10 units per 1,000 tokens, cached input 1 unit; - the cache holds between turns. If the context is byte-identical, turn one pays 200 units and the next nine pay 20 each: 380 units. If a timestamp near the top changes every turn, every turn pays 200: 2,000 units. The model also re-reads all 20,000 tokens every turn instead of reusing them, so each answer takes longer. Real ratios differ by provider; the mechanism is the same. ### Other reasons determinism matters - **Reproducible reviews.** A colleague who runs the same command on the same code sees exactly what the assistant saw. - **Meaningful diffs.** If saved context changes, the code changed, not a clock or a sort order. - **Trust.** A tool whose answers shift for no reason is hard to rely on. In the spec's words, "trust is the product". ## What dctx is not - **Not a type checker.** Call edges come from names, scopes and imports; ambiguous references are dropped. - **Not exact token counting.** Budgets use an estimate, `ceil(2 × UTF-8 bytes / 7)`, not a model's tokenizer. - **Not vector search or RAG.** No embeddings in the core, and the engine never calls a model. - **Not a hosted service or a daemon.** One binary that runs when you call it. No telemetry, not even opt-out. - **Limits still matter.** Plain `dctx pack` sends the selected project without an output budget by default. A 100 GB tree needs scoping, and the cache has a 2 GiB hard cap. CI covers Linux, macOS and Windows; byte-stability measurements here ran on Linux only. ## Where to go next - [README](../README.md): install, quick start, map mode. - [Specification](SPEC.md): rules, metrics, roadmap. - [Measurement evidence](BENCHMARK-20261030.md): grep plus file reads first; other-tool numbers are secondary historical notes. - [Stability report](research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md): protocol, raw answers and limits. - [Map mode guide](guides/MAP-MODE.md): every verb and option. ## Sources in this repository - [README.md](../README.md): core belief, map-mode budgets, MCP, `pack` tree lines, `--tree-stamps`, tested platform. - [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md): 1.1.0 prefix-stable `pack` output, stability re-measurement. - [docs/SPEC.md](SPEC.md): §2 rules PPE-1 to PPE-5, §3 defects R1 and R7, §4 privacy and no network, §11 page formats, §12.1 tiers, §13 token estimate, §32 non-goals. - [docs/research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md](research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md): 33/33 results and limits. - [docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md](BENCHMARK-20261030.md): `unresolved` call records. - Worked example and prefix figures: output of dctx 1.1.0 (`a4f6378`, built from [crates/dctx-cli](../crates/dctx-cli)) on a copy of [crates/dctx-lex-go](../crates/dctx-lex-go).

# Changelog

All notable changes to dctx are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). Dates are ISO 8601.

For current functionality and limitations, see the [README](README.md).
Historical entries describe the behavior and support scope of that release.
Current licensing: all first-party code and documentation, including the desktop app
and planned GPUI rebuild, are Apache-2.0, copyright Eris Margeta. Historical license
and distribution plans below do not describe the current release.

## [Unreleased]

## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-09

Install from the GitHub release archives. The npm, crates.io and PyPI packages and
the Go module are built and tested in CI, but registry publication is still pending;
until it happens, the release archives are the install path.

### Added

- `dctx rpc`: a versioned, newline-delimited JSON engine protocol over stdin/stdout
  (protocol 1.0.0, schema in `docs/protocol/`). Every reply carries `engine_version`;
  operation output is exactly the CLI stdout bytes.
- `dctx context TARGET...`: minimal ranked context for a file, symbol name or stable
  node id, with chunk ids, `--budget`, `--json` and `--session ID --dedupe`.
  `pack --for TEXT --json` now returns the same JSON context page.
- `dctx doctor [--json] [--probe-project]`: lists the dctx binaries visible from the
  current folder with path, ownership scope, version, build commit, SHA-256 and cache
  sizes. It changes nothing and uses no network.
- MCP `--profile lean|three` and `--tools NAME,...` select a smaller tool set with
  compact descriptions (lean start-up tool definitions: 6,278 -> 1,637 bytes). See
  [docs/guides/MCP.md](docs/guides/MCP.md).
- Python, Node (npm) and Go client packages over `dctx rpc`, each with CLI byte-parity
  tests in CI. They are not published to a registry yet.
- Release supply chain: keyless cosign signatures, CycloneDX SBOMs, GitHub build
  provenance attestations, a reproducible Linux musl build check and offline
  (air-gap) bundles. See [docs/VERIFYING.md](docs/VERIFYING.md). CI runs `cargo audit`.
  SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md describe the security and support policy.
- Robustness tests and a fuzz smoke workflow in CI.
- `dctx pack --for` prints a warning on stderr when the text names no identifiers;
  the page is unchanged.
- `dctx pack --clipboard` supports `xsel` on Linux.
- Experimental `tools/catalog-bench` for huge-tree catalog measurements (not part of
  the CLI).

### Changed

- `dctx pack` prints its `pack bytes=… files=… retention=… version=V1` status line on
  stderr. stdout is exactly the page and ends in a newline; `pack --json` stdout is
  exactly one JSON document. Scripts that read the status line from stdout must read
  stderr instead.
- Indexes live in an engine `major.minor` subdirectory of the cache parent
  (`DCTX_CACHE_DIR` or the platform `dctx/v2` root). 1.3 builds its own index on first
  use; patch releases share it, and older unscoped cache data is ignored, not deleted.
- Faster warm path: one fused inventory walk with directory-relative stats, rule files
  validated by stamps and cheaper decoding (measured checkout 288 -> 94 ms, 4k-file
  tree 88 -> 32 ms). Timestamp-only changes reuse the index generation.
- Each place keeps its own warm index; targeted queries no longer admit the whole
  place first; capacity errors name the exact limit and the flag that changes it.
- Pack output streams with bounded memory and spools large pages. Pack history uses
  compact manifest caches.
- Language extraction audit with new goldens; the default parser id is now
  `dctx-structural/3`.
- `dctx pack --for` keeps bare short names such as `main` and `run`, and keeps the
  case of capitalized words. Exact-case names and non-test code rank first, so
  `--for Session` finds the `Session` types before test functions.
- `dctx cache`, `dctx template`, `dctx context` and a bare `dctx` follow the exit-code
  contract in [docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md](docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md): 2 for usage errors,
  3 for I/O errors (naming the path), each with a `hint:` line. RPC `cache_status`
  returns the same codes. `dctx context` with no TARGET exits 2.
- A bare `dctx` whose stdin or stdout is not a terminal prints short usage and exits 2
  instead of starting the interactive menu.
- `dctx pack --help` prints only the pack usage and flags.
- `dctx plugin …` and `dctx git` text output is plain text. Refusals go to stderr as
  `❌ Error:` with a `hint:` line; a missing consent names
  `dctx plugin enable <id> --approve`. JSON output and exit codes are unchanged.
- `dctx cache auto` text shows a UTC time next to `last_auto_clean_ms` and
  `next_due_ms`; JSON is unchanged.
- Docs and package READMEs no longer present `npx dctx`, `npm install`,
  `cargo install dctx-cli`, `pip install dctx` or `go get` as working install paths.
  The Python missing-engine message no longer suggests a PyPI install.
- Bundled SQLite is 3.54.1 (rusqlite 0.41).

### Removed

- `dctx plugin run` and `dctx git` JSON replies no longer repeat the
  `facade_spawns` and `facade_git_children` keys. The facade counters remain once in
  `--json` output and are gone from text output.
- The cwd-relative plugin root fallback used when HOME was unset (see Security).

### Fixed

- Pack headers show `ID="UNIQUE_ID"` with clean quotes in the file-access
  instructions, including stamped and tree-only output. This changes pack output bytes.
- Pack rendering preserves literal template syntax in file bodies and paths, including
  backslashes, for default, stamped and compiled templates. Variable substitution
  applies only to template structure; `pack --for` also preserves source CRLF bytes.
- The last `</FILE_CONTENT_END …>` marker of a pack page is no longer glued to the
  status line.
- `dctx pack --for` with no usable terms says so and suggests backticks, instead of
  reporting that no name matched the index. Its flag refusal now lists `--json`.
- `dctx map` call edges stay within the caller's language family: a Rust `.all(..)`
  no longer resolves to a Makefile target. A guessed method call such as
  `iter.map(..)` links to a project method only when the caller can see that method's
  type. Hubs, neighbors, path and `pack --for` lose these false edges.
- `dctx plugin search` and the other text-mode plugin commands no longer mix JSON
  fields or internal counters (`facade_git= spawns= git_children=`) into the output;
  `dctx git status` without consent no longer prints `git: ConsentRequired`.
- `dctx pack --clipboard` with no clipboard tool names the tools it tried and suggests
  `--output FILE`.
- A symlinked or non-regular `.gitignore` or `.dctxignore` inside the project is
  skipped with a warning instead of failing the command; rule-file errors no longer
  print the absolute project path.
- Cache policy saves no longer get stuck on a `policy.v1.tmp` left by a crash.
- `dctx doctor` shows each binary's build commit (`commit:` in text, `"commit"` in
  JSON) and names an invalid argument.
- `dctx --help` lists `map export`; the `dctx map --help` examples map a file that has
  symbols.
- The Python wrapper raises `BinaryNotFoundError`, not `RuntimeError`, when no home
  directory is available (Windows without `USERPROFILE`/`LOCALAPPDATA`).
- Windows: durable file replacement, inode identity and racy-window directory stamps
  in map refresh. macOS: symlinked ancestors of the project, config and cache roots
  (such as `/var` and `/tmp`) are resolved at the boundary while in-tree symlinks stay
  refused; file names that APFS refuses are handled. Other cross-platform test and
  code fixes.
- README CLI reference, map-mode guide, modalities, start, testing and exit-code docs
  match the current binary and CI: all commands, 50 languages, neighbors depth 1..4,
  exact `--lines`, the global ignore file path, and that `.git/info/exclude` and
  `core.excludesFile` are not read.
- `tools/sync-version.sh` also syncs the Python, Go and npm package versions and the
  release links in the docs and package READMEs.

### Security

- Bundled SQLite upgraded to 3.54.1 (rusqlite 0.41, libsqlite3-sys 0.39.1) for
  RUSTSEC-2026-0459.
- Hardening across the engine and CLI, documented in
  [docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md](docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md).
- Pack and diff output entity-encode `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and control or line-separator
  characters in file paths, so a file name cannot forge file boundary markers.
  Ordinary paths are unchanged and output stays byte-stable.
- `dctx doctor` no longer executes dctx binaries found in `./node_modules/.bin`,
  `$VIRTUAL_ENV` or relative PATH entries, which an untrusted checkout can plant; they
  are listed with path and SHA-256. `--probe-project` opts in.
- MCP tool arguments are passed after `--` and taken literally, so a flag-shaped id or
  query (for example `--place`) cannot change the place outside the server root. MCP
  never forwards `--place` or `--output`.
- `pack --output`, `map export --output` and `template build --output` never follow a
  symlink or write into a non-regular target; pack and template write a fresh sibling
  file and rename it into place.
- Clipboard tools are looked up only in absolute PATH entries, so `.` or empty entries
  cannot run a repository's own `xclip` or `wl-copy`.
- The source reader checks an entry's type before opening it and never opens device
  nodes, FIFOs or sockets (Unix opens use `O_NOCTTY`). `StdFs` metadata, listings and
  link reads no longer follow symlinked path components; Windows ancestor guards block
  directory replacement.
- The store adapter refuses symlinked, foreign-owned or group/other-writable store
  roots and creates store directories with mode 0700.
- The plugin root no longer falls back to a directory relative to the working
  directory when HOME is unset; plugin commands refuse unless HOME or
  `DCTX_PLUGIN_ROOT` is an absolute path.
- The Python wrapper loads its `dctx_binary_<platform>` engine package only from the
  install directory that holds `dctx`, never from the working directory or other
  `sys.path` entries.
- The Python, Node and Go package READMEs warn that operation arguments carry full CLI
  authority.
- The website playground rate limit can no longer be bypassed with a forged
  `X-Forwarded-For` header. The website deploy builds without secrets and deploys only
  from `main` through a protected environment; the desktop release workflow is
  disabled until the desktop app ships, with pinned toolchains, a frozen lockfile and
  provenance attestations.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-06

Release **1.1.0** (`v1.1.0`; release candidate `v1.1.0-rc1` 2026-11-04). It folds in the 1.0.1 line, which was never released on its own.

### Since rc1 (docs, CI, tooling and SPDX licence headers only; no change to dctx output)

- **Docs**: byte stability re-measured on 2026-11-06 — 33/33 text and 33/33 JSON map answers identical
  after unrelated edits and over five runs (see docs/research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md);
  SPEC and README status texts updated, historical 0/63 kept.
- **Formal**: the plugin TLC gate accepts the newer TLC wording 'Temporal property X was violated.' /
  'Invariant X was violated.' (all 8 baselines, 59 mutants, 37 witnesses pass); host-specific
  tla2tools.jar paths removed; TLC trace files ignored.
- **Self-hosted CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): the job run step by step on a self-hosted Linux runner (16 cores) from a clean
  `git archive` of the commit; results and badge recorded in `docs/ci/RESULTS.md` — 2279 run, 2279 passed, 0 skipped.
- **Third-party npm licence inventory**: `scripts/npm_licenses.py` indexes every repository `package-lock.json` into
  `THIRD_PARTY_NPM.md`; `npm_licenses.py --check` runs in CI and fails on a disallowed licence or a stale report.

### Added

- **Perl** (`.pl`, `.pm`, `.t`, `.psgi`): `package A::B;` and `package A { .. }` as `type` symbols holding every later
  `sub` (named `A::B::name`) as `fn` symbols (`guess` confidence, full tier). POD is masked like a comment; call edges
  come from `name(..)`, bareword calls with an argument and `&name`, never after `->`, `sub` or a sigil.
- **Fortran** (`.f90`, `.f95`, `.f03`, `.f08`, `.f`, `.for`): `module`, derived `type` and named `interface` as `type`
  symbols; `program`, `function` and `subroutine` as `fn` symbols named `module::name` (`guess` confidence, full tier).
  Keywords are case-insensitive, `!` comments only, fixed-form column rules are not modelled; call edges skip
  intrinsic and control keywords that precede `(`.
- **Verilog/SystemVerilog** (`.v`, `.vh`, `.sv`, `.svh`): `module`, `macromodule`, `interface`, `package` and `class`
  declarations as `type` outline symbols and `function`/`task` declarations as `fn` symbols (`guess` confidence, full tier),
  with module-scope call edges and `<module> <instance> (` instantiation links resolved through the call index.
- **Prefix-stable `pack` output**: tree lines carry the `ID` only, with no `MOD:` and no `SIZE:`, so a
  bare `touch` leaves the page byte-identical and an edit keeps everything before the edited file as a shared prefix
  for prompt caches. `--tree-stamps=on|off` (default `off`) selects the built-in tree template; `on` reproduces the
  1.0.0 bytes. The desktop tree-only export keeps its digest line last, behind a stable lead line.
- **Stat stamps in the manifest**: a stamp pass runs before the digest, with a racy-timestamp guard; a
  touch-only change is decided by content. A gate replays 200 random edits against a cold rebuild.
- **Record and entry caps**: checked during the scan and set by `DCTX_MAX_RECORDS` and
  `DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES`; the cache is reclaimed on publish, evicts before refusing, and readers share one lock.
- **Open-source maintenance model**: `MAINTENANCE.md`, `TRADEMARK.md`, a DCO in
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `FUNDING.yml`; the desktop app is open source too.

### Changed

- **Id lookup** uses a sorted hash index instead of a linear node scan.
- Large source files were split into submodules by pure moves (400-line rule): `pack.rs`, `path.rs`, `reuse.rs`,
  `bound.rs`, `plugin.rs`, `yaml.rs` and others. No behaviour change.
- The version is **1.1.0** for every `crates/*` and `plugins/*` package; the desktop app stays on 0.11.0.

### Fixed

- A closed stdout pipe (`dctx pack | head`) exits 0 without a panic.

## [1.0.0] — 2026-10-31

The first v1 release, folded from the 0.26 development line. Every `crates/*` and
`plugins/*` package, `VERSION`, `project-meta.yaml` and the README badge are at **1.0.0**
(`tools/sync-version.sh --check` keeps them and their `Cargo.lock` entries together). The
desktop app keeps its own version line (0.11.0) and its own release workflow.

### Shipped surface
- **Map verbs**: `dctx map map | find | neighbors | explain | read | skeleton | grep | hubs | path | export`,
  with hard token budgets, stable ids, cursor paging and precision labels; call and import edges are lexical.
- **`dctx mcp`**: a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools.
- **`dctx pack`**: the whole project as one structured block to stdout, the clipboard or `--output`.
- **`dctx pack --for "<text>" --budget N`**: task context for an agent card: `map find` on the names the text mentions,
  then neighbors and read of the best hits, whole lines only, within N estimated tokens (ceil(2 × UTF-8 bytes / 7),
  default 3000). `tools/cardgen/context.sh` prepends it to a card; `docs/guides/AGENTS-SNIPPET.md` is the `AGENTS.md` section that tells agents to run it first;
  `tools/cardgen/dogfood.py` records before/after prompt tokens for the ten v1 cards.
- **`dctx languages`**: one registry with three tiers (full, outline, docs) that also renders the README table.
- **Privacy deny**: sensitive files (env files, keys, credentials, ...), `.git` at any depth and symlinks are
  never read or printed by `pack`, any map verb or `mcp`; there is no override flag. Detection is by file name only.
- **Determinism**: two fresh indexes give byte-identical answers, and an unrelated edit changes only `hubs`;
  `scripts/release-check.sh` gates both, and counts network syscalls under `strace -f` (must be zero).
- **`dctx --version`** prints `dctx 1.0.0 (<git sha>)`; the sha is embedded at build time, `unknown` without git.
- **README benchmark section** rendered from the committed run 7 JSON by `scripts/render_readme.py`;
  `just readme-check` fails when the README differs.

### Out of scope for v1
- Any network or cloud feature.
- macOS and Windows support claims (untested); Linux x86_64 is the only tested platform.
- Watch or incremental mode beyond re-indexing.
- Fortran and Verilog (both shipped in 1.1.0).
- Shell call edges.
- Embeddings and semantic search.
- LSP-grade type resolution.
- A stable plugin ABI and desktop API (unstable, not a v1 contract).
- Cross-repository queries.
- Publishing to crates.io or GitHub (a maintainer decision).

### Added
- **Call and import edges** in the map index: `dctx map neighbors --edge calls|imports`
  now answers who calls what, resolved by lexical scope, imports and module paths, with
  `name`/`guess` confidence; ambiguous references are dropped.
- **New map verbs**: `skeleton <file>` (declaration signatures, no bodies), `grep <literal>`
  (hits grouped by enclosing symbol), `hubs` (most-called symbols and per-directory counts),
  `path <FROM> <TO>` (shortest edge path) and `export --format json|mermaid` (the whole graph).
  `neighbors --depth` goes up to 4 (breadth-first, each node once).
- **`dctx mcp`**: a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools.
- **`dctx languages`** (`--json`, `--markdown`): every supported language with its tag, file names, tier
  (full: symbols and lexical call edges; outline: symbols only; docs: sections) and confidence, from one facade
  registry (`dctx::LANGUAGES`) that also feeds `--version --verbose` and the README table, which a test diffs.
- **A CLI exit-code contract** (`docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md`) for `map`, `pack`, `mcp`, `languages` and unknown
  commands: 0 ok, 1 no result (an id not in the index, a binary file target, nothing to pack), 2 usage, 3 index
  error. Every failure prints a `hint:` line. Previously every failure exited 1. A non-UTF-8 argument is now a
  usage error instead of a panic, an unknown flag is named as unknown, and `dctx map <verb> --help` prints a page
  with an `Example:` line for each map verb.
- **Outline symbols (`guess` confidence) for 25 more formats**: Scala, Dart, Zig, Solidity,
  Gleam, Groovy; Elixir, Lua, OCaml, R, Julia, Haskell; Terraform/HCL, SQL, shell, Makefile,
  Dockerfile, protobuf, Pascal, GraphQL; and headed sections for `.txt`, `.rst`, `.adoc`,
  `.org` and `.tex` documents.
- **A three-way benchmark against graphify and Trail-Code** (`docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md`)
  and the gap matrix behind it (`docs/GAP-MATRIX-20261030.md`).

- **dctx Desktop is free, forever** for individuals, teams and companies
  ([announcement](https://dctx.app/news/desktop-free-forever/)).
- **The dctx Context Management Specification** (`docs/SPEC.md`): prompt-processing
  efficiency as the core belief, the ten RAG defect classes and how dctx rules
  them out, the seven-layer organization policy, prefix-stable tiers and delta
  answers, the persistent index, the plugin boundary and the roadmap.
- **An isolated, reproducible benchmark against Trail-Code**
  (`docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/`): methodology, raw data, scripts and
  numbered findings.
- **Map mode** (`dctx map`): `map`, `find`, `neighbors`, `explain` and `read`
  with hard token budgets (up to 2,000 per answer), cursor paging, stable ids,
  explicit `moved`/`gone`/`ambiguous` outcomes and precision labels on every answer.
- First-party structural extractors for JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Python, Go,
  Java, C/C++, C#, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Markdown and JSON/TOML/YAML; Rust
  through `syn`.
- A verified map generation reused across CLI invocations.
- **Plugin host**: capability grants, consent, receipts, liveness by progress,
  signed distribution verified with Ed25519, and Linux confinement; the bundled
  **Git plugin** (`.gitignore` protection and consented staging).
- **Cache lifecycle**: time-based expiry, a system size cap and a bounded
  automatic cleaner (`dctx cache status | gc | purge | config | auto`).
- `dctx pack`: an explicit pack to stdout, the clipboard or `--output`, without
  leaving files in the project.
- The template system's v2 compiler (a sealed plan IR) and organization ceilings.
- `crates/dctx`: one library facade for the CLI, the desktop app and future
  bindings.
- A new website with changelog and news, and the dctx film
  (`presentation/video/`).

### Changed
- **Byte-stable map answers**: the text header is `# <place> <verb>` and JSON no longer
  carries `snapshot`, `generation` or `freshness.age_s`, so answers stay identical across
  unrelated edits (prompt-cache friendly). `--meta` restores the old fields.
- **`dctx pack` never prints env-shaped files** (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`, `.envrc`); they
  stay in the tree by name with their content omitted.
- **Strict sensitive-file deny for every command**: besides env files, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore`, SSH private keys (`id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, ...),
  `credentials`, `credentials.json`, `secrets.yaml` (and other data extensions), `.npmrc`,
  `.netrc`, `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`, `.htpasswd` and `.git-credentials` are never read or printed
  by `pack`, any `dctx map` verb (by id or raw path, with or without `--in`) or `dctx mcp`.
  There is no override flag (see ADR-014).
- **`.git` is closed for good**: a `.git` segment at any depth is never listed or read by the map
  verbs and never read by `pack`, even when `.gitignore` or `.dctxignore` says `!.git/`.
- **No symlink escapes**: `FsSource` opens files with `O_NOFOLLOW`, requires a regular file
  handle, and refuses symlinked directories, so a symlink swapped in after the stat cannot leak
  bytes from outside the root.
- `DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1` (ignore files are not applied) is now documented in ADR-014; the
  sensitive-file deny, the `.git` guard and the symlink rules still apply when it is set.
- **Total-source ceiling raised from 64 MiB to 1 GiB**; `DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` overrides it.
- The core never reads `.git/`, never spawns `git` and never uses VCS object ids;
  content identity is dctx's own SHA-256 (`crates/dctx-hash`).
- Repository ignore rules are applied before any read on the map path, and
  `--lines A-B` returns exact line ranges.
- Everything in the repository is licensed under Apache-2.0.

### Fixed
- Node spans resolve from one newline index per file instead of rescanning the
  source for every symbol (cold `find` on a 3,000-file repository: 141 s → about 6 s).
- Queries share one generation instead of cloning it (peak memory down by about
  30 % on the same repository).
- One hostile file no longer fails every map verb for the whole repository: a Rust
  file that is not UTF-8 is indexed as a module with no symbols (like every other
  language), and a file name the confined path cannot carry (a backslash) is skipped
  and marks the snapshot `partial`, as `pack` already did.

### Known issues
Measured in the benchmarks and scheduled in the specification's roadmap:
- No incremental indexing: the first query after an edit re-indexes, and each
  edit adds a full generation to the cache.
- Outline-tier formats carry symbols and `contains` edges only; heuristic families are
  labelled `guess`. `dctx languages` lists the tier and confidence of every format.
- The 70-question task protocol (run 7: 140/140) was designed by the dctx team; an
  independently selected protocol (v1 card 6) is pending.

# Contributing to dctx

Read the [specification](docs/SPEC.md), [crate map](docs/CRATE-MAP.md) and
[Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before making changes. Project contributions
are licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE), consistent with [NOTICE](NOTICE).

## Bugs, ideas and questions

Search existing [issues](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/issues) before opening
one. Use the bug or feature template and keep reproductions small. Include the
commit or version, OS/architecture, build features, exact command, expected result
and actual result. Redact source code, paths, credentials and generated context
that you do not have permission to share.

Report suspected vulnerabilities privately using [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md),
rather than in an issue or pull request. For other questions, open an issue with
what you tried and the relevant documentation link.

## CLI development setup

Use a recent stable Rust toolchain with Cargo; the workspace includes Rust 2024
crates. Clone the repository and run commands from its root:

```zsh
git clone https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx
cd dctx
cargo build --locked -p dctx-cli
cargo run --locked -p dctx-cli -- --help
```

Cargo builds **`dctx-cli`**, while help text calls the tool **`dctx`**. See
[installation](README.md#installation) for aliases and install choices.

Keep changes focused on the relevant crates and preserve unrelated work. The
[`dctx` facade](crates/dctx/) serves the CLI and the desktop API; pure engine
crates should not acquire filesystem, network or process effects. The
[plugin guide](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md) describes effect boundaries and current
runtime limitations.

## Validation

Start with the CLI and facade checks (some tests validate documentation):

```sh
cargo test -p dctx-cli -p dctx --locked
```

For documentation changes, install the Python dependencies using
[the website setup](tools/website/README.md), then run
`tools/website/.venv/bin/python tools/check-markdown-links.py`. It checks local
paths and heading anchors across public Markdown, including HTML and reference links.
[Testing](docs/TESTING.md) documents the full Linux/macOS/Windows matrix and
local commands. The current [CI workflow](.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs workspace
tests on stable Rust and MSRV, plus formatting, Clippy, Rust documentation,
licence, website and release checks. Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and document
public APIs. Follow [Rust house style](docs/STYLE.md) for the plugin boundaries.

When editing website source documents, regenerate `website/` and check it using
[the website instructions](tools/website/README.md). Before committing, use
`check.py --working-tree` to compare your regenerated files with an independent
build; CI compares committed output. Capture CLI examples only if output changed.

Desktop changes need their platform prerequisites and separate validation; see
[the desktop guide](apps/dctx-desktop/README.md). The root `just ci` recipe also
invokes desktop setup and is broader than the main CI jobs.

## Developer Certificate of Origin

Contributions use the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org)
(DCO) instead of a contributor license agreement. Sign off each commit to certify that
you wrote the change, or otherwise have the right to submit it under Apache-2.0:

```zsh
git commit -s
```

The `-s` flag adds a `Signed-off-by:` line with your name and email. Pull requests with
unsigned commits will be asked to amend them with `git commit --amend -s`, or to rebase
with `--signoff`.

## Pull requests

Create a focused branch from `main` and describe the problem, resulting behavior
and any compatibility or privacy impact. Add regression coverage for behavior
changes and update affected documentation. Check Markdown links and paths when
editing guides. Use clear commit messages, for example `fix(cli): reject empty
output paths`.

In the PR, list the commands you ran, their results, and any checks you could not
run. Include relevant OS/build features for platform-specific changes. Avoid
unrelated formatting, generated governance files, local caches, credentials and
private research artifacts. Maintainers may ask for a smaller change or additional
validation before merging. Pull requests, including forks, run on GitHub-hosted CI runners.

# dctx maintenance

dctx is open source under the Apache-2.0 license and free for any use, including commercial use. A maintenance agreement is how organisations that depend on dctx pay for its upkeep. Paying never changes the license and never closes a feature.

## What an agreement covers

- **Security fixes.** Response targets are counted from the moment a report is confirmed:
  - Critical: a fix or mitigation within 72 hours.
  - High: a fix within 7 days.
  - Medium: a fix in the next release.
- **Long-term support.** The 1.x line receives backported fixes for 18 months after 2.0 is released.
- **Priority on bug reports.** Reports from covered organisations are triaged first.
- **A say in the roadmap.** Covered organisations can propose priorities in a regular review. The maintainer keeps the final decision.
- **Advance notice of breaking changes.** You hear about a breaking change before it ships, with a migration note.
- **Invoice and written commitment.** You receive invoices and a signed maintenance commitment for procurement and vendor review.

Security reports still go through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), whatever your tier.

## Tiers

| Tier | Who it is for | What you get |
|------|---------------|--------------|
| Supporter | Individuals and teams who want to fund dctx | Sponsorship and your logo in the README. No service commitments. |
| Team | One organisation that depends on dctx | Everything under "What an agreement covers", for one organisation. |
| Partner | Organisations that build products on dctx | Team, plus integration help and a named contact. |

Supporter sponsorship runs through [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/Eris-Margeta). Team and Partner agreements are arranged directly.

## Pricing and contact

Pricing on request: info@tejl.com

Write to that address with your organisation, the tier you want and a contact name.

## Guarantees

- Paying never changes the license. dctx stays Apache-2.0 for everyone.
- Paying never closes or paywalls a feature. Every feature stays in the open source project.
- The core (`pack`) and every modality stay open.

**System binary — available now.** Download the archive for your OS and architecture
from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/releases/tag/v1.3.0),

`dctx` (`dctx.exe` on Windows) on `PATH`. Archives cover Linux x64/ARM64,
macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64. Releases after 1.2.0 also ship cosign signatures,
a CycloneDX SBOM, build provenance and offline bundles; see
[verification, provenance and offline installation](docs/VERIFYING.md).

```sh

```

**Project wrappers — built and tested in CI, registry publication pending.** The
[Python](packages/python/README.md), [Node](packaging/npm/dctx/README.md) and
[Go](packages/go/README.md) wrappers over `dctx rpc` are built and tested in CI,
but nothing is published to PyPI, npm, crates.io or a Go module proxy yet. Until
then, a `dctx` package on those registries is not from this project. The
[Rust facade](docs/MODALITIES.md#rust-library-embed-the-facade) is available from
tagged Git. Use the release archives for the CLI.

for one project, lean MCP setup and whole-session measurement.

## Start and choose your path

[What dctx is](docs/START.md), [four user paths](docs/START.md#choose-your-path),
[responsibilities](docs/START.md#responsibilities), and
[two scopes, one binary](docs/START.md#two-scopes-one-binary) explain setup and
ownership. The [documentation index](docs/README.md) groups modalities, scopes,
engine behavior, reference material, trust and evaluator evidence.

“Smallest correct context” is the goal: selection is lexical and bounded, not a
proof of task completeness or a mathematical minimum. Large folders need scoped
roots; budgets bound answers, not scans. Provider cache hits and whole-session
savings must be measured. See [current limits](docs/MODALITIES.md) and the
[specification and roadmap](docs/SPEC.md).

## The core belief: prompt-processing efficiency

Send fewer relevant bytes, keep their order stable, and verify exact source.
dctx does not use embeddings; it selects lexical symbols and document sections.

- **Bounded**: map answers use estimated token budgets and whole records.
- **Deterministic**: identical source snapshots and requests give identical bytes.

Read the [philosophy](docs/WHY-DCTX.md) and its
[testable constraints](docs/SPEC.md#2-the-core-belief-prompt-processing-efficiency).

<!-- library:begin -->
```rust
use dctx::{memory::{CancelFlag, FixedClock, MemorySource}, *};
let mut source = MemorySource::new();
source.insert_file("hello.rs", b"pub fn hello() {}\n", 0)?;
let mut session = Session::builder(source).clock(FixedClock(Timestamp(0)))
    .cancellation(std::sync::Arc::new(CancelFlag::new())).ceiling(HostCeiling::base())
    .selection(SelectionPolicy::from_texts(&RuleTexts::default())).grants(HostGrants::PermitAll)
    .storage(StoragePolicy::Ephemeral { max_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }).place("demo").view("pack").build()?;
```

### Language tiers


`dctx languages` prints this table (`--json` for tools, `--markdown` for this block) from the one registry that also drives `dctx --version --verbose`; a test fails when the block below differs from it.

- **full**: symbols and call edges. Call edges are lexical, not type-resolved: they come from names, scopes and imports, never from a type checker, and ambiguous references are dropped.
- **outline**: symbols only; no call edges are promised. Shell function bodies can yield same-file call guesses, but v1 does not promise shell call edges.
- **docs**: headed sections.
- **Confidence**: `guess` marks the heuristic outline families, and every record from those files carries confidence `guess`; `structural` means a dedicated lexer or deterministic document rules.

## Security & Privacy

Pack, map and MCP run locally and have **no telemetry**, **call no model** and
**make no network calls**. Selection happens before any byte is read, hashed,
parsed or cached, and is checked again before output leaves the engine.

| Rule file | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `.gitignore`, `.dctxignore`, global ignore file | Excluded from normal selection; `--debug-ignored` shows ignored path metadata without reading content |

The global ignore file is `<config dir>/dctx/ignore`: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dctx/ignore`
or `~/.config/dctx/ignore` on Linux and macOS, `%APPDATA%\dctx\ignore` on Windows.
dctx does not read Git metadata, so `.git/info/exclude` and Git's
`core.excludesFile` are **not** applied: copy those patterns into `.dctxignore` or
the global ignore file when they must keep files out of a pack.

`DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1` skips those ignore texts, so leave it unset when relying
on them. Built-in sensitive-file and `.git` exclusions still apply.

Sensitive files such as `.env`, private keys and credentials are omitted from
content reads even with ignore negations; pack may list their names.
`.git` at any depth is never listed or read by map, and is never read by pack.
Symlinks are never followed; final-component file opens use `O_NOFOLLOW`.
dctx decides by file name only: a secret pasted into an ordinary source file
is not detected. Inspect context before sharing it.
The [privacy contract and deny list](docs/ADR-014-Privacy-Guarantees-and-Ignore-Semantics.md)
and [map privacy guide](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md#index-cache-and-privacy) explain
the boundary. Report vulnerabilities privately through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

The [release check](scripts/release-check.sh) tests socket activity under
`strace -f` and reports SKIP where tracing cannot run. Plugin network and
organization policy designs in the spec include planned features;
see [current plugin limits](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md#what-is-not-yet-available).

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

The current major release receives bug fixes and security fixes in its latest
release. When a new major is released, the previous major receives security fixes
for **six months after the new major's release date**, then reaches end of support.
Older majors receive no fixes. Upgrade to the latest patch within a supported
major before checking whether an issue is resolved. We publish fixes in new patch
releases; we do not promise a separate patch for every historical minor version.
This public policy has no LTS commitment beyond that six-month transition. Include the exact
version or commit and build features so maintainers can assess affected versions.

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Do not disclose vulnerabilities in public issues or pull requests.** Use
[GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/security/advisories/new)
or email [info@tejl.com](mailto:info@tejl.com) with a subject beginning
`[dctx security]`. If GitHub's private reporting form is unavailable, use email.
Maintainers must enable private vulnerability reporting in repository security
settings; that GitHub setting is separate from this policy file.

Include, where possible:

- Affected version or commit, OS/architecture and build features.
- The affected component and potential impact (for example ignored-file content
  disclosure, untrusted plugin execution, or signature verification bypass).
- Exact reproduction steps and a minimal synthetic fixture or proof of concept.
- Expected and actual results, with sanitized diagnostics.
- Whether the issue has been shared elsewhere, and a preferred contact method.
- A name or alias for credit, or a request to remain anonymous.

Never send private keys, tokens, production data or a generated context export
containing confidential code. Use synthetic examples and redact sensitive values.
Test only systems and data you own or have explicit permission to assess.

## What counts as a vulnerability

dctx is an offline tool, but untrusted repositories, files, archives and plugin
inputs still cross security boundaries. Report issues such as:

- Disclosure of ignored, excluded or secret-file contents, including through
  generated context, caches, diagnostics or plugin access.
- Arbitrary code execution, sandbox or capability bypass, unsafe plugin execution,
  or command injection caused by processing untrusted input.
- Path traversal, symlink escapes, unintended file modification or unsafe archive
  extraction outside an authorized destination.
- Signature, checksum, provenance or update verification bypass; compromised
  release artifacts or dependencies affecting supported builds.
- A reproducible resource-exhaustion attack from a small malicious input that
  defeats documented bounds and makes the tool unusable.

Ordinary output mistakes, unsupported language coverage, feature requests and
performance issues without a security boundary impact belong in public issues.
Use private reporting when unsure. Offline operation does not make confidential
local data or the release supply chain out of scope.

## Handling and disclosure

We acknowledge private vulnerability reports **within 7 days**. We investigate
impact, identify affected supported versions and coordinate a fix or mitigation
and public disclosure with the reporter. Remediation timing depends on severity
and available maintainers; the acknowledgment window is not a promised fix deadline.
If acknowledgment has not arrived within 7 days, follow up through the other
private channel. Credit is subject to the reporter's consent.

We will not take legal action against individuals who discover and report
security vulnerabilities in good faith and in accordance with this policy.

Please coordinate public disclosure so users can receive a fix or mitigation.
For architectural boundaries and current implementation limits, see the
[README](README.md#security--privacy) and [plugin guide](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md).
Those descriptions are not a security certification.
